claims.explanation: Vinorelbine is a tubulin-polymerization inhibitor, so selectivity is most plausibly driven by the cellular context that determines mitotic spindle dependence and drug efflux/response. The strongest recurring pattern is that lines with intact p53/RB and EGFR- or BRAF-driven oncogenic signaling (e.g., EGFR-mutant NSCLC, BRAF-mutant melanoma, PTEN-loss breast/endometrial lines) are enriched among sensitive lines, whereas lines with additional resistance-associated alterations such as STK11, SF3B1, or high-level multidrug-efflux/EGFR-independent contexts are enriched among the least affected lines. Because the provided abstracts do not directly report vinorelbine pharmacogenomics, these features are inferred from the observed selective-killing pattern and general tubulin-inhibitor biology rath

features.basis: Most sensitive lines carry TP53 mutations, consistent with impaired mitotic checkpoint/apoptosis favoring spindle-poison activity
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines (NCIH1650) are among the most killed; EGFR signaling can increase mitotic dependence
BRAF-mutant melanoma/endometrial lines (IGR37, K029AX, HEC265) are enriched in the sensitive set
PTEN loss in ZR751, HEC265 and other sensitive lines may increase PI3K/AKT-driven mitotic entry
STK11-mutant lines (SNU840, KALS1) appear among least affected, suggesting reduced dependence on microtubule dynamics
SF3B1-mutant lines (UO31, HCC95) are among the least affected, possibly via altered splicing of tubulin/mitotic genes
NF1-mutant lines appear in both extremes but enriched in least-affected set, suggesting RAS/MAPK-driven resistance
RB1-mutant lines (OV7, GSU, FTC133) are enriched among least affected, consistent with bypass of mitotic arrest
High TUBB3/beta-III tubulin is a known mediator of resistance to tubulin-polymerization inhibitors
Multidrug efflux pump expression reduces intracellular vinorelbine and is a canonical resistance mechanism
MAP2K1-mutant NCIH1437 is among least affected, suggesting MAPK-pathway activation can bypass spindle stress
KMT2D mutations recur in several sensitive lines (HEC265, KU1919, KE39, BICR6), possibly via chromatin-mediated mitotic gene regulation
